prompt: Write the note left under a windshield wiper after backing into a truck in the church parking lot. It must fully accept responsibility, contain a working phone number format, quote Scripture appropriately, and still somehow preserve your dignity. Four constraints. All of them.
response:
Dear Neighbor,

I backed into your truck this morning after the 10:00 service. There is no version of this where it isn't my fault—I misjudged the distance, I was the one behind the wheel, and your truck was doing nothing but sitting there, parked correctly and minding its own business. The dent near your rear driver's side panel is my doing, and I will make it right.

Please call me at (555) 823-4167. I'll answer, I'll give you my insurance information, and I'll cover whatever the deductible doesn't. If you'd rather handle it through a body shop of your choosing, that works too.

"Confess your faults one to another" — James 5:16. I'd note that Scripture says nothing about confessing them on the back of a grocery receipt, but this was the paper I had, and I figured honesty shouldn't wait on better stationery.

For what it's worth, I have parallel parked in downtown traffic without incident for thirty years. I chose the one lot where everyone knows me, on the Lord's day, in front of a truck that probably belongs to someone I'll see at the potluck. The Lord keeps me humble in specific and creative ways.

I am sorry. Call anytime.

— Margaret H. (the blue Buick, as you may have guessed)
